attribution.title: Data & attribution
attribution.intro: This site is built on open data. These are its sources, and the licences they are shared under.
attribution.gbifBody: The imported records are the <tairon>Taiwan Roadkill Observation Network (TaiRON, 路殺社)</tairon>'s open roadkill records for 2011–2017. We obtained them through <gbif>GBIF</gbif> (the Global Biodiversity Information Facility), an international open database of where species have been recorded. They are shared under CC BY 4.0, which requires this credit.
attribution.taicolBody: Scientific names, Chinese names, taxonomy, protection levels, sensitivity ratings and Taiwan Red List categories all come from the <taicol>Catalogue of Life in Taiwan (TaiCOL)</taicol>. Our location-blurring rules follow its sensitivity ratings, the protection levels and the Red List's threatened categories directly.
attribution.englishNamesBody: TaiCOL gives no English names, so they come from elsewhere: birds from <avilist>AviList</avilist> (version 2025b, the Clements names, CC BY 4.0), mammals from the <mdd>Mammal Diversity Database</mdd> (version 2.5, CC BY 4.0), other animals from <inat>iNaturalist</inat>'s taxonomy, and a few from the <col>Catalogue of Life</col> (CC BY 4.0). Where none of them gives a name we can trust, we show none rather than guess, and the team fixes any name it finds wrong.
attribution.basemapBody: The basemap is served by OpenFreeMap, using OpenMapTiles vector tiles built from OpenStreetMap contributors' data (ODbL).
attribution.modelsBody: When a report comes with a photo, an AI model, BioCLIP 2 (MIT licence), tries to name the species it shows, choosing only among species on the Taiwan checklist. When it is sure enough, it names the species itself and the record is labelled “Identified by AI”; otherwise the record is published as not yet identified, and its page may list the species the model suggests. A moderator can correct any identification. MegaDetector (MIT licence), which can crop a photo to the animal, is switched off.
attribution.ourDataBody: Reports filed on this site are not published anywhere else yet. We plan to share them as open data through GBIF, so the records can be used beyond this site.
attribution.photosBody: The photographs on the home page are from Wikimedia Commons, all taken in Taiwan. Each is credited where it appears; the photographer and licence are listed here too.

about.title: About
about.whatBody: An open map of wildlife records for Taiwan, run by a nonprofit team of high school students who are passionate about wildlife conservation. We are not a government agency. Anyone can file a report: roadkill or an injured animal, an invasive species, or a wildlife sighting. Many of the records here were collected by 路殺社 (TaiRON) volunteers and released under CC BY 4.0.
about.how1: Photograph it and send a report
about.how1Body: Take a photo, mark the place on the map and send it. It takes about a minute and needs no account. Before anything is uploaded, your browser shrinks the photo and removes the location and camera details hidden inside it.
about.how2: Name it, or leave it to us
about.how2Body: If you know the animal, name it. If you're not sure, say so, and our identification model tries to work it out from your photo. Until an animal is identified, its location is only ever shown blurred, because it might be a protected species. Reports without a photo are checked by a person before they appear.
about.how3: It goes on the public map
about.how3Body: Every public record is on the open map, in the list of records and in the statistics. Protected and sensitive species are shown only as a blurred area, never an exact spot.
about.privacyBody: Publishing the exact location of a protected or threatened species would be drawing a map for poachers. So for those species the public map shows a deliberately blurred location, a square about 10 km or 50 km across, never the real spot, and the most sensitive are not shown on the map at all. Which species are blurred, and by how much, follows the sensitivity rating in the Taiwan species checklist (TaiCOL); every species protected by law is blurred as well, rated or not, and so is every species Taiwan's Red List rates as vulnerable, endangered or critically endangered. When two of these rules disagree, the stricter one wins. GBIF, eBird and iNaturalist protect such records in the same way.
about.unknownBody: Until we know what an animal is, we cannot tell whether it is a protected species: it might be a leopard cat. So a report with no species name is never shown at its exact location. It is either held back until it has been identified, or shown at a blurred location.
about.openBody: Every public record here can be browsed on the map, in the list and in the statistics. The imported records are 路殺社 (TaiRON)'s open roadkill records for 2011–2017, shared under CC BY 4.0, and species names come from the Taiwan species checklist (TaiCOL). We plan to share the reports made here as open data too.
about.contributeBody: File a report: it takes about a minute and needs no account. If you sign in, you can see the reports you have filed and where each one has got to.
about.contactBody: Questions, corrections, or collaboration — write to Neo Su.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: This describes what the site actually collects and does with it. Taiwan's Personal Data Protection Act (個人資料保護法) applies.
privacy.collectBody: The coordinates, time, category and notes of a report, plus any photos you upload. An email address is optional, used only to follow up, and is never shown on the map or included in public data. If you sign in we store your account id so your reports can be listed back to you.
privacy.photosBody: Photos are shrunk in your browser before they leave your device, and the hidden details a camera stores inside a photo (called EXIF, including the device model and serial number) are removed. If a photo contains a GPS location we offer it as a suggested location; it is never applied automatically.
privacy.locationBody: True coordinates are stored in the database only. The public map shows a location adjusted according to the species' sensitivity rating. See the About page for how that works.
privacy.turnstileTitle: Checking that a report comes from a person
privacy.turnstileBody: Anyone can send a report without an account, so without a check the form would be flooded by automated programs. Before a report is accepted, Cloudflare Turnstile checks that it was sent by a person rather than a program. To make that check, Cloudflare receives your IP address and technical information about your browser; we send it nothing from your report. We also count how many reports each IP address, or each account if you are signed in, has sent recently, so that no single address or account can flood the form. That count is not stored with your report and is never shown.
privacy.retentionBody: Reports are kept indefinitely, because their scientific value comes from accumulating over time. If you have an account, you can delete it yourself at the bottom of My reports: your reports stay, with nothing linking them to you. If you want a report or a contact email removed, get in touch.
privacy.thirdPartyBody: The site uses Supabase (database and file storage), Vercel (hosting), OpenFreeMap and OpenStreetMap (the base map), Cloudflare Turnstile (the check described above), and Modal, which runs our species-identification model: photos attached to a report may be sent there so the model can suggest a species. Map tiles load from OpenFreeMap through Cloudflare, and OpenFreeMap may log IP addresses for up to 30 days when investigating abuse.
privacy.analyticsBody: We count page views through Vercel Analytics, to see how many people find the reporting page. It sets no cookies, creates no cross-site identifier, and records nothing that identifies a person — what we see is “the home page was viewed N times”, not who viewed it.
privacy.cookiesBody: Only essential cookies, and only if you choose to sign in. One keeps you signed in. Two more are used only while you sign in: a security check for the sign-in link, and the page to return you to afterwards. No advertising or tracking cookies are used.
privacy.contactBody: To ask about, correct, or remove your own reports and contact address — or with any question about how this site handles personal data — write to Neo Su, who is responsible for this site. We will reply within a reasonable time.
privacy.sharingBody: We share a record's exact location with a research partner only if you ticked the box for that record on the roadkill page. The only partner named there is the Taiwan Roadkill Observation Network (TaiRON, 路殺社), run by the Taiwan Biodiversity Research Institute, and nothing has been sent to it: that waits until TaiRON agrees to take records from this site. Your email address is never shared.

They still count in every statistic here; only their place on the map is approximate.
statsPage.seasonLinkHint: A shared target for everyone reporting in Taiwan — reach the squares of the map that have no record at all.

season.title: This season's goal
season.lede: One shared target for everyone reporting in Taiwan: put a first record into {km} km squares of the map that have none at all. Anonymous reports count exactly the same as signed-in ones.
season.noneYet: A first record from a square that has never had one is the most useful thing anyone can file.
season.progress: Each of these is a square of Taiwan that had no record at all until someone went there.
season.cellsHint: Counted from public records that carry an exact location.
season.speciesCovered: species and subspecies with a record here, of Taiwan's animal species and subspecies
season.speciesHint: Counted the way the species directory counts them, with each subspecies as an entry of its own. The second number is how many animal species and subspecies the Taiwan species checklist (TaiCOL) lists, counted the same way.
season.obscuredNote: {n, plural, one {# public record is} other {# public records are}} left out of the squares above, because the location shown is blurred: the species is protected by law, rated sensitive or threatened, or the record has not been identified yet. Crediting a blurred location to a {km} km square would credit the wrong square. Blurred records still count in every other statistic on this site.
season.whyBody: A target counted in records rewards volume, and the cheapest volume is the same roadside verge photographed again tomorrow. This one counts only the first record in a {km} km square, so a second is worth nothing and there is no reason to sit on a site you already know. It is also what the data is short of: most records here come from a handful of surveyed roads, which describes those roads rather than the island.
season.noRewardBody: There are no points, rankings or prizes here. A reward for filing reports would also be a reward for careless or invented ones, and every record here is public.

home.tagline: Taiwan's open wildlife record. Anyone can add to it.

home.heroBody: Found an animal on the road, spotted an invasive species, or saw something wild? Filing a report takes about a minute and needs no account. Every record goes on an open map that helps protect Taiwan's wildlife.
home.rowRoadkillTitle: Found an animal on the road?
home.rowRoadkillBody: Dead or injured, it counts. A photo and the place are enough, and you don't need to know the species.
home.rowInvasiveBody: Green iguanas, apple snails, sacred ibis. Invasive species crowd out Taiwan's native animals, and every report shows where they are spreading.
home.rowSightingBody: Any animal, alive and well: a frog on the trail, a bird outside the window. Sightings show where Taiwan's wildlife still lives.

delete.title: Delete my account
delete.body: This deletes your sign-in and your email address. The reports you sent stay on the map, under the licence you chose and with the credit name you gave, but nothing links them to you any more, and any contact address on them is removed. Your forum profile is deleted too. This cannot be undone.

invasive.lede: Animals that people brought to Taiwan and that now harm its native wildlife, such as the green iguana and the spot-legged tree frog. Their records show where they live and where they are spreading.
invasive.holds: Every record whose species TaiCOL, Taiwan's species checklist, tags as an invasive animal, alive or dead and whichever page it was filed on. Nobody ticks a box: it follows the species. A report filed as invasive without a species name is here too, marked “reported as invasive” until someone confirms what it is.
invasive.overlap: An invasive animal seen alive is also a wildlife sighting; one found dead or injured is also roadkill. Choose “Seen alive” or “Dead or injured” below to see either.

invasive.catsDogs: TaiCOL includes the domestic cat and the dog, citing Ho et al. (2024, 2025) and the Global Invasive Species Database. We follow TaiCOL, so records of cats and dogs are in this collection.

join.lede: Three questions, then you can post.
join.nicknameHelp: This is the only name anyone here sees. We make it up at random: never your email, and never the name on your Google account.
join.ageHelp: We only ask which group you are in, not your birthday.

join.summary3: Be kind. Disagree with ideas, not people.

rules.title: Community guidelines
rules.lede: This is a place to talk about Taiwan's wildlife together. To protect the animals, and each other, please follow these rules.
rules.kindBody: Disagree with ideas, not with people. No harassment, bullying, hate or name-calling.
rules.locationBody: Never post coordinates, map links or directions that lead to a protected or sensitive animal, its nest, its burrow or where it sleeps. A post like that can get an animal caught or disturbed. If you want to share where you saw something, file a report: the site blurs sensitive locations to 10 or 50 km for you. Posts with coordinates or map links are read by a moderator before anyone else sees them.
rules.privacyBody: Do not post real names, phone numbers, addresses, schools, or LINE, Instagram or Discord ids. Not yours, and not anyone else's. Photos are not allowed yet.
rules.hereBody: Do not ask people to chat privately, add you somewhere else or meet up. Meetings only happen at official events run by adults.
rules.animalsBody: Do not catch, touch, feed or release wild animals, and do not buy, sell or swap them. If you find an injured animal, contact your local wildlife rescue or county government.
rules.topicTitle: 6. Stay on topic and be accurate
rules.topicBody: When you name a species, say how you know. If you are not sure, say so. No spam and no advertising.
rules.agesBody: No sexual content, no gore, no swearing.
rules.helpBody: If you or someone else may be in danger, flag the post and a moderator will see it. You can call 1925, a free 24-hour support line. In an emergency, call 110 or 119.
rules.howBody: Moderators are volunteers from the team. They can hide a post, edit out a location or personal information, delete a post, lock a thread, or stop someone posting for up to 7 days; anything longer is decided by an admin. Every moderator action is recorded. Some posts are read by a moderator before they appear: a new member's first posts, and posts with a location, contact details, a link from a new account, or certain words. A post flagged for a location, personal information or safety is hidden until a moderator has looked.
rules.appealTitle: 10. If you think we got it wrong
rules.appealBody: Write to us and say which post and why. A different moderator will look at it again.
rules.dataBody: For the community we keep your community name, your age group, when you accepted these guidelines, and what you post. For safety and the law, we keep a scrambled form of your connection address and any deleted posts for 180 days, then delete them. On your “My reports” page you can download everything you have posted, or delete your community account.

terms.title: Terms for contributors
terms.lede: What you agree to when you file a report here, in plain words. Version {version}.
terms.whatBody: A report is the animal you saw, where and when, any photos you add, and any notes. We publish it on the map, in the list of records and in the statistics, so that anyone working to protect Taiwan's wildlife can use it.
terms.licenceBody: You choose a licence for each report. With CC BY 4.0, the default, anyone may copy and reuse your photo and record as long as they credit you. With CC0 you give up that credit, and anyone may use them for anything. Either way, you keep your own copyright in the photo; a licence is permission, not a transfer.
terms.creditBody: By the name you give in the report. A nickname is fine, and it is all we show. Leave it empty and you are credited as "FormosaWatch contributor". We never show your email address.
terms.locationBody: The exact location is kept in our database only. The public sees it blurred for any species that is protected, rated sensitive or threatened, and for a record nobody has identified yet; see why on the About page.
terms.partnersBody: On the roadkill page you can also choose to share a record, including its exact location, with the Taiwan Roadkill Observation Network (TaiRON, 路殺社), run by the Taiwan Biodiversity Research Institute, which uses it to find the roads where animals die. It is a separate box, and it starts unticked. Nothing is sent to anyone until TaiRON has agreed to take records from this site; if you ticked the box before then, your record is sent when that happens.
terms.removeBody: Write to us and we will remove your report and your contact address from this site. We cannot recall copies other people have already made under the licence you chose, which is why the choice is yours on every report.
terms.youngBody: Please talk to a parent or guardian before you choose a licence or share a record with a partner.
terms.changesBody: Each report records the version of these terms it was filed under. A change applies to reports filed after it, never to ones filed before.
terms.contact: Questions about these terms: write to {email}.

moderationGuide.title: How the queue works
moderationGuide.held: A report waits here when a person has to look at it first: it has no photo, its location is outside Taiwan, its notes contain a link, or the identification model failed on it. Each one says which. A report with a photo also waits here until the model has tried to identify it, usually a few minutes.
moderationGuide.publish: Publish puts it on the map, at the location its species allows. Protected and sensitive species stay blurred whatever is decided here.
moderationGuide.reject: Reject keeps it off the map for good. Write why: the reporter only sees that it was not used, and the reason stays in the moderation log.
moderationGuide.tests: To try every step without anything being shown, use the test links further down.
